derivation.item: Why constant collapsed electric mass is excluded
derivation.proof: For fixed real h let C=||h||^2/256, or C=||h||^2/128 for complex h. An electric measure carrying fixed positive weight w at energy1/n has inverse moment at least n w, contradicting the uniform bound C for large n. Thus such a constant-norm collapsing electric atom cannot occur under these premises. E4/TOTAL convergence alone, without the uniform inverse theorem, would not exclude it.

The nonnative exact family mu_n=(1/(256n)) delta_(1/n) obeys finite inverse integral1/256 for every n and converges in TOTAL mass to the zero measure: its total norm squared is1/(256n)->0. Its limiting inverse moment is0, not1/256. For every fixed K, integral fK dmu_n=(1/(256n))min(K,n)->0, consistently with the continuous-zero argument. Therefore the inverse upper bound passes, but inverse-weight mass need not be conserved. The associated weighted finite measure dmu_n/E has mass1/256 that collapses tozero energy; it must not be identified with the inverse-weight measure of the limiting zero source. This is a spectral method countercontrol, not a claimed native spectrum.
